title: RAG
summary: The retrieval layer RAG depends on (ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector and hybrid search), then grounded generation and advanced RAG architectures.
outcome: Build and evaluate a complete RAG system, from retrieval infrastructure to grounded, cited answers that abstain when evidence is thin, and choose architectures by failure mode.

project.title: Hybrid Search Engine + Advanced RAG Application
deliverables: Ingest, clean, chunk, embed and index a real corpus with metadata in a vector database
Implement dense, BM25 and hybrid retrieval with metadata filters, served as a search API or UI
Document Q&A app with ingestion, chunking, retrieval, generation, citations and abstention
A baseline RAG pipeline plus at least one real improvement (reranking, query transformation, RAG-Fusion, hybrid or an advanced variant)
Graceful handling of weak retrieval and insufficient evidence
Track latency, token usage and cost across the pipeline
Deploy as an API or simple UI

modules.title: Data ingestion & document processing

topics.d: Pull content from common formats and know when OCR is needed.
Normalize messy text while preserving structure and metadata.
Handle duplicates, document updates and incremental re-indexing.

modules.outcome: Turn a real document collection into clean, structured data ready for retrieval.

modules.title: Chunking strategies

topics.d: Why documents are split before embedding and retrieval.
Four families of chunking methods.
How each affects retrieval quality.
Small precise chunks vs larger chunks with more context.

modules.outcome: Choose a chunking strategy from document structure and query type.

modules.title: Embeddings fundamentals

topics.d: Vectors that capture semantic relationships.
Embedding documents and queries with an embedding model.
Dimensions, multilingual/domain quality, cost and latency.
Embeddings from different models are not comparable.

modules.outcome: Select and use an embedding model suited to a retrieval task.

modules.title: Similarity & semantic search

topics.d: How each measure compares vectors.
Query → embedding → similarity → top-k without a vector DB.
Meaning-based vs exact keyword matching.
Exact names, IDs, numbers and rare terms.

modules.outcome: Build semantic search without a vector database and know what a DB will automate.

modules.title: Vector databases & ANN search

topics.t: Storing vectors in pgvector or Qdrant
topics.d: Embeddings, documents, IDs and metadata in a vector DB.
Vector queries combined with metadata filters.
Brute force gets expensive at scale; ANN trades exactness for speed.
Speed, memory and recall trade-offs.
Index maintenance and operational basics.

modules.outcome: Build and query a scalable vector index over a real corpus.

modules.title: Sparse & hybrid retrieval

topics.d: Keyword retrieval with BM25 and when it beats embeddings.
BM25-style sparse vs vector-based dense retrieval.
Merging dense and sparse results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
Names, IDs and exact phrases benefit most.

modules.outcome: Choose dense, sparse or hybrid retrieval instead of defaulting to vectors.

modules.title: Capstone: Build a Hybrid Search Engine

topics.t: Ingest, chunk, embed & index a real corpus
topics.d: Clean corpus with metadata, indexed in a vector DB.
All three retrieval modes with useful filters.

topics.t: Deploying a search API or UI
topics.d: Serve the most relevant chunks through an API or UI.

modules.outcome: A hybrid retrieval system ready to be a RAG app's retrieval component.

modules.title: RAG architecture & when to use it

topics.d: Query → retrieve → assemble context → generate.
Private knowledge, changing information, large corpora and sourced answers.
When the model already knows enough or the data fits in context.
Telling the two kinds of failure apart.

modules.outcome: Decide whether a problem genuinely needs RAG.

modules.title: Baseline RAG from scratch

topics.d: A full RAG pipeline on top of your retrieval system.
Top-k chunks into the prompt, then a grounded answer.
Keep answers tied to supplied evidence.
Respond sensibly when retrieval is weak or irrelevant.

topics.t: The effect of k and chunk ordering
topics.d: How k, order and context size shape quality.

modules.outcome: Build working RAG without hiding the mechanics behind a framework.

modules.title: Reranking

topics.t: Retrieve many, rerank, send the best
topics.d: Two-stage retrieval: wide recall, then precise reordering.
Cross-encoders and dedicated rerankers.
Weighing relevance gains against latency and cost.
Measuring with and without reranking.

modules.outcome: Improve the context sent to the LLM without just retrieving more.

modules.title: Query transformation & RAG-Fusion

topics.t: Why the user question is a poor query
topics.d: Raw questions often retrieve poorly.
Rewriting, expansion, multiple queries and hypothetical document embeddings.
Multiple queries, retrieval for each, rankings fused with RRF.
Multi-query for ambiguous or multi-part questions.
Extra LLM calls, latency and cost.
Skip it when baseline retrieval already works.

modules.outcome: Turn hard user questions into better retrieval queries.

modules.title: Grounding, citations & abstention

topics.d: Answers based on retrieved evidence, not unsupported knowledge.
Link claims to supporting chunks with useful citations.
Verify that cited sources really support the claim.
Detect weak evidence and say so honestly.
Separate retrieved evidence from model synthesis.

modules.outcome: Produce traceable answers that abstain when evidence is insufficient.

modules.title: RAG variants & advanced patterns

topics.d: From naive to advanced to adaptive, self-correcting RAG.
Retrieve when needed and reflect on evidence and output.
Grade retrieved evidence and correct when it is weak.
Decide dynamically whether and how to retrieve.
Repeat retrieval and generation until evidence suffices.
Questions that need several retrieval steps or sources.
Retrieval over entity and relationship graphs.
Connected knowledge, global questions and cross-document info.

topics.t: Choosing by failure mode, not novelty
topics.d: Compare variants by the failure they fix and their cost.

modules.outcome: Choose a RAG architecture based on why the baseline fails.

modules.title: RAG with frameworks

topics.d: Recreate the hand-built pipeline with a framework.
Framework abstractions for ingestion, retrieval and citations.
Reranking and query transformation via components.
Control, speed, debugging and complexity compared.

modules.outcome: Use RAG frameworks productively while understanding what is underneath.

modules.title: Capstone: Deploy an Advanced RAG Application

topics.t: A document Q&A app end to end
topics.d: Ingestion, chunking, retrieval, generation, citations and abstention.

topics.t: A baseline plus one real improvement
topics.d: Baseline, then reranking, RAG-Fusion or similar.
No bad failures when evidence is thin.
Measured across the pipeline.

topics.t: Deploying as an API or UI
topics.d: Ship it as an API or simple interface.

modules.outcome: A complete RAG application that goes well beyond retrieve-stuff-generate.
